analyst_view.overall: Early view: Juventus (5th, 10 points) are well placed for a top-eight finish, although Luciano Spalletti's side remain uneven in Serie A (2-2 at home to Fiorentina, rescued by Bremer, before the break). Omonia (18th, 6 points) have lost their last two European games after a bright start under Henning Berg.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals. I lean higher: Juventus's European games have produced 15 goals in four (5-0, 2-1, 2-2, 2-1), and Omonia have conceded seven in their last two (1-4 to Benfica, 1-3 at NEC). With Nick Woltemade and Randal Kolo Muani both scoring, 3-0 or 3-1 looks more likely than a narrow win.

corners.text: The numbers say 11.0 corners, 8.1 of them for Juventus. That is high, and Juventus had few corners at AZ, but they will have far more of the ball at home against Omonia, so I stay close to the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards. A home game Juventus are expected to control should be calm, and Omonia are more likely to sit in than to scrap, so I stay with a low count.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.9 shots, which is a lot. Spalletti's side have been efficient rather than high-volume in Europe, building a two-goal half-time lead at AZ from few chances, so I lean lower, around 27.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 shots on target. Juventus's finishing has been sharp and Omonia have let in seven goals in two games, so I see no reason to move away from about 10.
